name: coordinate-grid
title: Coordinate grid
tagline: Numbered coordinate grid: points, segments and lines x = k / y = k / y = mx + c, labels derived; place-point, select-point and place-line (draw the line) answers.
description: A coordinate grid with numbered axes, optional plotted points (labelled, with optional coordinate readouts), line segments between points, axis-parallel constant lines (x = k / y = k) and straight lines in slope-intercept form (y = mx + c), each drawn across the whole grid with a derived equation label. Ranges crossing zero produce a four-quadrant grid automatically. Supports answer-on-the-model questions (marked model tile): place-point (click a grid intersection), select-point (tap a rendered point), and place-line (draw a straight line by dragging the two handle points of a pre-placed wrong line; the placeLine param names the target and marking derives from it — any two distinct points on the correct line pass).
whenToUse: Any teaching about coordinates, plotting, position or straight lines drawn on a grid. Use with points: [] for a blank answer-space grid ("plot the point (3,2)"); with labelled points + showCoordinates for worked examples; with occlude: true on a point to hide its readout as (?, ?) for practice questions; with negative ranges for four-quadrant work. Use lines for full-grid lines — lines: [{x: -1}] draws the vertical line x = −1, lines: [{y: 6}] the horizontal line y = 6, and lines: [{m: 2, c: 1}] the straight line y = 2x + 1 (write x + y = 4 as {m: -1, c: 4}); set occlude: true on a line to hide its equation as "?" for "what is the equation of this line?". For a "draw the line …" QUESTION use a marked model tile with responseMode "place-line", correctAnswer { derived: true } and placeLine naming the target ({m: 2, c: 1} | {x: -1} | {y: 6}) — do NOT also author the same line in lines (that would draw the answer); a given companion line (simultaneous equations) does go in lines. Choose axis ranges so the target line crosses the grid well inside the window (for y = mx + c make sure at least two grid intersections on the line are in range — handles snap to axes.step). Constant/straight lines differ from segments, which join two named points. On wide ranges number the axes in 2s or 5s (axes.labelStep) rather than every line — cramped tick numbers are never acceptable. Keep axis ranges identical across blocks in one lesson so the representation stays stable for pupils.

x.description: [min, max] for the x-axis, e.g. [0, 10] (first quadrant) or [-5, 5] (crosses zero → four quadrants).

step.description: Grid spacing in axis units (the x grid, and the y grid unless yStep overrides). Default 1. Also the snap grain for place-point clicks and place-line handles.

yStep.description: Grid spacing for the y-axis alone, when the printed grid counts up faster than across — a draw-the-graph window like y −16…14 over x −2…3 has 1 square = 1 unit across but 2 units up, so set step 1 with yStep 2. Keeps the squares near-square on a tall window (the canvas already compresses a tall y-axis to stay readable) and becomes the y snap grain. Default: step.

labelStep.description: Number the axes every this many units while the grid stays at step — e.g. step 1 with labelStep 2 or 5 counts in 2s/5s. Use a multiple of step. Governs both axes unless yLabelStep overrides. Default: every grid line is numbered, which CROWDS on wide ranges — if a range spans more than ~15 units, set labelStep so numbers stay clearly separated.

yLabelStep.description: Number the y-axis every this many units, when it needs a different count from x (x every 1, y every 2). Use a multiple of yStep. Default: labelStep.

grid.description: Show grid lines. Default true. Set false for a sparser sketch look.

label.description: Point name shown beside the marker, e.g. "A". Omit for an unnamed point.

occlude.description: Hide this point's coordinate readout as "(?, ?)" when showCoordinates is on — the question hook for "what are the coordinates of…?". The marker and label stay visible.

color.description: Optional CSS colour for the marker. Default is the theme accent.

points.description: Points to plot. Empty/omitted = blank grid (an answer space).

segments.description: Line segments between labelled points, as pairs of point labels, e.g. [["A","B"],["B","C"]]. Useful for shapes and journeys. For a full-grid line (x = k / y = k / y = mx + c) use lines, not segments.

lines.description: Full-grid lines, each drawn across the whole window with a DERIVED equation label. Each item is EXACTLY ONE of: {x: k} (vertical line x = k), {y: k} (horizontal line y = k), or {m, c} (the straight line y = mx + c, clipped to the grid; write x + y = 4 as {m: -1, c: 4}). Use for "draw the line …" figures and, with occlude, "what is the equation of this line?". A line that misses the grid window is not drawn. For a marked "draw the line" QUESTION use placeLine instead — a lines entry would draw the answer.

x.description: Draw a VERTICAL line at this x value (the line x = k), spanning ymin..ymax. Provide exactly one of x / y / m.

y.description: Draw a HORIZONTAL line at this y value (the line y = k), spanning xmin..xmax. Provide exactly one of x / y / m.

m.description: Gradient of a straight line y = mx + c, drawn across the grid. Pair with c (c defaults to 0). Provide exactly one of x / y / m.

c.description: y-intercept of the straight line y = mx + c. Only meaningful with m. Default 0.

label.description: Override the derived equation label (default "x = k" / "y = k" / "y = mx + c"). Rarely needed — only for a non-equation caption.

showLabel.description: Show the equation label beside the line. Default true; set false for an unlabelled line.

occlude.description: Hide the equation label as "?" (the line itself stays visible) — the question hook for "what is the equation of this line?". Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the line and its label in the amber result/emphasis colour. Default false.

m.description: Target gradient: the pupil must draw y = mx + c. Pair with c (default 0). Provide exactly one of m / x / y.

c.description: Target y-intercept for the m form. Default 0.

x.description: Target VERTICAL line: the pupil must draw x = this value.

y.description: Target HORIZONTAL line: the pupil must draw y = this value.

placeLine.description: The place-line TARGET — the line the pupil must draw ({m, c} | {x} | {y}). Question tiles only: pair with responseMode "place-line" and correctAnswer { derived: true }. The target is the question ("Draw the line y = 2x + 1" — put the equation in the header or stem), so it is public. Static surfaces (print/PPTX) draw NO line for it — a blank answer space; on web/slides a complete but WRONG line is pre-placed as two draggable handles that snap to the grid, and marking derives from this spec: any two distinct committed points on the target line are correct. Choose ranges so at least two grid intersections on the target line sit well inside the window.

highlight.description: Labels of points to emphasise with a ring (draws the eye in worked examples).

showCoordinates.description: Render "(x, y)" readouts beside labelled points. Default false. Combine with per-point occlude for question variants.

header.description: Optional short title rendered above the grid.

draggable.description: Web-only: points can be dragged, snapping to the grid, with live coordinate readout. Use for exploration ("move A to (5, 1)"); has no effect on static surfaces. Ignored when the tile carries a responseMode.

examples.label: Worked example — plotted points with readouts
Wide range numbered in 2s (unit grid, uncrowded labels)
Constant line — the vertical line x = −3 (four quadrants)
Constant line — the horizontal line y = 4
Hard case — the lines x = 2 and y = −3 crossing on four quadrants
Straight line — y = 2x − 1 drawn and labelled (worked example)
Question — name this straight line (occluded y = mx + c)
Hard case — simultaneous pair y = x + 1 and y = −2x + 7 with the intersection read out
Draw the line y = 2x + 3 — place-line question state (marked model tile: responseMode "place-line", correctAnswer { derived: true }; statically a blank answer space)
Draw the line x = −2 — place-line question state (vertical target on four quadrants)
